name: Barbados

registry.name: Corporate Affairs and Intellectual Property Office (CAIPO)

legalStatuses.label: Registered business name
legalStatuses.plain: You run the business as an individual under your own name or a business name. You and the business are the same person for tax. Usually the simplest way to start.

legalStatuses.label: Limited company
legalStatuses.plain: The company is its own legal person, separate from you. It costs more to set up and has more paperwork, but it can limit your personal risk.
legalStatuses.feeNote: A company costs more to set up than a business name. The registry will quote you the current fees.

launchSteps.label: Get your TIN (Taxpayer Identification Number) from the BRA
launchSteps.plain: A number that identifies you to the tax office. You need it for almost every other step.

launchSteps.label: Choose your business name and check that it is free
launchSteps.plain: If you trade under any name other than your own, you must register it. Reserve it with CAIPO first.

launchSteps.label: Register the business name, or incorporate the company, with CAIPO
launchSteps.plain: Online or in person. For a business name, approval usually takes about five working days.

launchSteps.label: Register with the National Insurance Office (NIS)
launchSteps.plain: Self-employed people must register and contribute. It gives access to a pension and other benefits.

launchSteps.label: Register with the BRA and plan your advance tax payments
launchSteps.plain: Self-employed people pay income tax in advance, each quarter, and file a yearly return by April 30.

launchSteps.label: Open a separate bank account for the business
launchSteps.plain: Keeping business money apart from household money makes your numbers clearer and your taxes easier to pay.

launchSteps.label: Register as an employer and prepare monthly payments
launchSteps.plain: With employees you pay income tax (PAYE) and NIS each month, by the 15th of the following month.

launchSteps.label: Register for VAT
launchSteps.plain: Required once your taxable sales pass the VAT threshold. Register with the BRA.

incomeTax.label: Income tax
incomeTax.bracketText: 11.5% on the first BDS$50,000 above the allowance, then 27.5%

corporateTax.label: Corporation tax
corporateTax.note: Since 2024 the standard rate is 9%. A company registered as a small business under the Small Business Development Act, with gross income of BDS$2 million or less, pays 5.5%.

contributions.label: NIS and related funds
contributions.plain: National Insurance and related funds (pension, health, training). Self-employed people pay 17% of insurable earnings, up to BDS$5,360 a month.

contributions.label: Resilience and Regeneration Fund
contributions.plain: A fund for climate and disaster resilience. It applies to all earnings, with no ceiling.

vat.label: Value Added Tax
vat.registerNote: Plan to register once your sales reach BDS$200,000. The March 2026 budget raised the level to BDS$350,000 from 1 October 2026: the BRA confirms the level that applies to you when you register.
vat.filingNote: Your filing period is set when you register.

calendar.quarterlyTextPersonal: Pay your advance income tax instalment (prepayment), based on last year's tax. The balance is due by April 30. NIS for the self-employed follows its own schedule: ask the National Insurance Office.
calendar.quarterlyTextCorporate: Companies prepay 50% of last year's tax in one or two instalments, depending on the year-end, then pay the balance with the return: the BRA gives you your dates.
calendar.annualTextPersonal: File your income tax return for the year before.
calendar.payrollText: Every month: pay income tax (PAYE) and NIS for the previous month.
calendar.vatText: If you are registered for VAT: file your return for each period. Your period is set when you register.

toVerify: VAT registration threshold: BDS$200,000, raised to BDS$350,000 from 1 October 2026 by the March 2026 budget according to two reports; no confirmation from the Barbados Revenue Authority found
Corporation tax: 9% since 2024 (5.5% for registered small businesses up to BDS$2 million) according to Parliament papers, while the BRA corporations page still shows the older sliding scale
